facts.raw_span: a two-year history of gradually progressive abdominal distension
denied pain, vaginal bleeding, or systemic symptoms
no personal or family history of cancer
BMI was 20.5 kg/m2
blood pressure 125/85 mmHg
pulse 89/min
SpO2 95% on room air
abdomen was markedly distended with a palpable mass rising approximately 3 cm above the umbilicus
Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated an 18 cm diameter ovarian tumor
hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL with a microcytic profile (MCV 73.2 fL)

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a large, fluid-filled lesion measuring 19.3 × 6.2 × 21 cm, located in the pelvis and mid-abdomen, displacing the uterus and compressing the aorta and inferior vena cava
a two-year history of gradually progressive abdominal distension
denied pain, vaginal bleeding, or systemic symptoms
no personal or family history of cancer
BMI was 20.5 kg/m2
blood pressure 125/85 mmHg
pulse 89/min
SpO2 95% on room air
abdomen was markedly distended with a palpable mass rising approximately 3 cm above the umbilicus
Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated an 18 cm diameter ovarian tumor
hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL with a microcytic profile (MCV 73.2 fL)

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a large, fluid-filled lesion measuring 19.3 × 6.2 × 21 cm, located in the pelvis and mid-abdomen, displacing the uterus and compressing the aorta and inferior vena cava

concepts.why: The large, fluid-filled ovarian tumor with a unilocular appearance and no septations or solid components is consistent with a mucinous cystadenoma of the ovary.
The large, fluid-filled ovarian tumor with a unilocular appearance and no septations or solid components could also be consistent with a serous cystadenoma of the ovary.
Although less likely, the ovarian tumor could be an ovarian fibroma, which can also present as a large, fluid-filled mass.
The presence of a large ovarian tumor and microcytic anemia could be consistent with a dysgerminoma, a type of ovarian germ cell tumor.
The large ovarian tumor and microcytic anemia could also be consistent with an immature teratoma of the ovary, a type of ovarian germ cell tumor.

rationales.F01: Abdominal distension is a common symptom of ovarian tumors.
rationales.F03: No personal or family history of cancer reduces the likelihood of malignant ovarian tumors.
rationales.F08: A palpable mass in the abdomen is consistent with a large ovarian tumor.
rationales.F09: Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrating an ovarian tumor strongly supports ovarian tumor diagnoses.
rationales.F11: Elevated HE4 levels are associated with ovarian tumors, particularly epithelial types.
rationales.F12: CT scan findings of a large, fluid-filled lesion in the pelvis and mid-abdomen are consistent with a large ovarian cystadenoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Large, fluid-filled ovarian tumor with elevated HE4 level and no solid components, consistent with a mucinous cystadenoma.
